commitments.quote: It applies to all agreements under which Business Associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits Protected Health Information for or on behalf of Covered Entity (the "Underlying Agreements").
commitments.summary: The BAA applies to every agreement under which ExampleCo creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI for Covered Entity.
commitments.scope: All agreements under which Business Associate handles PHI for Covered Entity (the Underlying Agreements).
commitments.deviation: The BAA reaches all PHI handled under any Underlying Agreement, while the DPA covers only processing of Customer Personal Data under the Agreement.

commitments.quote: Terms used but not defined in this BAA have the meanings given in the HIPAA Rules (45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164), including "Breach," "Discovery," "Protected Health Information" ("PHI"), "Electronic Protected Health Information" ("ePHI") and "Unsecured Protected Health Information."
commitments.summary: Undefined terms, including Breach and Discovery, take their meanings from the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.scope: Breach, Discovery, PHI, ePHI and Unsecured PHI as defined in the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.deviation: The BAA defines breach and PHI by reference to the HIPAA Rules, while the DPA defines Personal Data by reference to applicable Data Protection Laws and sets its own confirmed-breach standard in 1.3.

commitments.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
commitments.summary: Security Incident covers only incidents involving ePHI that ExampleCo or its Subcontractors handle for Covered Entity.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving ePHI created, received, maintained or transmitted by Business Associate or its Subcontractors for Covered Entity.
commitments.deviation: The DPA's Personal Data Breach requires a breach ExampleCo has confirmed, while the BAA uses HIPAA's broader Security Incident concept limited to ePHI and does not require confirmation.

commitments.quote: "Subcontractor" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103.
commitments.summary: Subcontractor takes the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103.
commitments.scope: Entities that are Subcontractors under HIPAA.
commitments.deviation: The DPA defines Subprocessor as any third party engaged by ExampleCo that processes Customer Personal Data, while the BAA uses the HIPAA definition of Subcontractor.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use and disclose PHI only as necessary for the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as the BAA permits.
commitments.scope: PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA limits use and disclosure to necessity, legal requirement or the BAA, while the DPA limits processing to Customer's documented instructions and has no legal-requirement exception.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.scope: PHI.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may de-identify PHI only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and may use the result only to provide and improve the services.
commitments.scope: PHI de-identified under the HIPAA safe harbor method.
commitments.deviation: The BAA allows de-identification only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and use only to provide and improve the services, while the DPA allows use of Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.

commitments.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
commitments.summary: Information de-identified under Section 2.3 falls outside PHI and outside the BAA.
commitments.scope: Information de-identified under Section 2.3.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no express exclusion for de-identified data; by inference, its limit to Customer Personal Data in 2.1 produces a similar result.

commitments.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
commitments.summary: A limited data set is treated as PHI for every purpose of the BAA.
commitments.scope: Limited data sets under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule for ePHI.
commitments.scope: ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule for ePHI, while the DPA requires implementing the Annex 2 measures and permits updates that do not materially reduce security.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.scope: PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows offshore access, including from Manila, under the Annex 3 transfer mechanism, while the BAA prohibits storage, processing and access outside the United States with no transfer mechanism.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires HITRUST r2 for PHI systems, while the DPA requires a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the Services.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and no later than 10 calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery, as defined in the HIPAA Rules and not restated in this BAA (inference: the clock runs from when Business Associate knew or should reasonably have known of the Breach)

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI as defined in the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires notice within 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach, while the BAA gives 10 calendar days after Discovery with no confirmation requirement.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Security Incident involving ePHI within 5 business days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becomes aware of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving ePHI as limited by Section 1.2.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives notice only of confirmed Personal Data Breaches within 72 hours of confirmation, while the BAA requires notice of every Security Incident involving ePHI within 5 business days of awareness.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: Unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts are treated as noticed by Section 4.2 and need no further report.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes unsuccessful attempts from Personal Data Breach, including log-in attempts, pings, port scans and denial-of-service attacks, while the BAA lists only pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts and treats them as noticed.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by the BAA within 10 calendar days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becoming aware of the use or disclosure

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.summary: Reports under Section 4 must be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office, with a copy to its Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example
commitments.scope: All reports under Section 4.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the Services console or to the account owner, while the BAA requires written reports to named Privacy Office and Information Security Office email addresses.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: A Breach report must include, to the extent known, each affected individual's identity, the PHI involved, the dates of the Breach and of its Discovery, and mitigation steps.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity, under Section 4.4 (Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, copy to iso@ahs.example)
commitments.scope: Reports of a Breach.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires a description of the nature of the breach, the data categories and the measures, while the BAA also requires the identity of each affected individual and the dates of the Breach and of Discovery.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media about a Breach it or its Subcontractors caused.
commitments.scope: Breaches caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must ensure each Subcontractor handling PHI agrees in writing to the same restrictions that apply to ExampleCo.
commitments.scope: Subcontractors that create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on Business Associate's behalf.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires a written flow-down of the same restrictions to each PHI Subcontractor, while the DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessor performance but has no written flow-down requirement.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within 10 business days after its request.

deadline.anchor: Covered Entity's request

commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary for compliance review.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA gives the HHS Secretary direct access to records, while the DPA routes regulator-required audits through a customer-conducted on-site audit limited to one per year on 60 days' notice.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days after termination of the Underlying Agreements.

deadline.anchor: Termination of the Underlying Agreements

commitments.scope: All PHI.
commitments.deviation: The BAA requires return or destruction of all PHI within 30 days, while the DPA requires deletion within 90 days, allows backups 35 further days, and provides certification only on request.

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: If return or destruction is not feasible, ExampleCo must keep applying the BAA protections to the retained PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.scope: PHI that cannot feasibly be returned or destroyed.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
commitments.summary: The VDPA overrides the Subscription Agreement and any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
commitments.scope: Covers all of the VDPA's terms, not only processing of personal data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 11.1 gives the DPA priority only for processing of Customer Personal Data; this VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over Vendor and Affiliate data processing terms, policies and online terms generally.

commitments.quote: means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
commitments.summary: Retailer Data covers all data Retailer, its employees or customers provide or that Vendor collects from Retailer systems, including telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and derived data.
commitments.scope: Defines the data covered by every Retailer Data duty, including derived data and telemetry.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 1.1 covers only Personal Data in Customer Data; this VDPA covers all Retailer Data, including non-personal telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and derived data.

commitments.quote: means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
commitments.summary: A Data Incident is any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including incidents at a Subprocessor.
commitments.scope: Covers actual or reasonably suspected incidents involving any Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 1.3 covers only breaches Vendor has confirmed that affect Customer Personal Data; this VDPA covers actual or reasonably suspected incidents involving any Retailer Data, including at a Subprocessor.

commitments.quote: means any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
commitments.summary: A Subprocessor is any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
commitments.scope: Includes Vendor Affiliates as Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 1.4 defines a Subprocessor as a third party engaged by ExampleCo; this VDPA expressly includes any Vendor Affiliate.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.summary: Vendor may process Retailer Data only to provide the Services and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.scope: Applies to all Retailer Data as defined in Section 2.2.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 2.2 allows processing on instructions set out in the Agreement, the DPA and Customer's configuration; this VDPA limits processing to providing the Services and Retailer's written instructions.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to serve Retailer.
commitments.scope: Covers any machine learning model and all Retailer Data, including derived data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 8.1 bars training only foundation models made available to other customers and allows Usage Data use under 8.2; this VDPA bars training or improving any machine learning model except one used only for Retailer.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.summary: Vendor may store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.scope: Covers storage of Retailer Data; the contract does not address access from other locations.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 6.1 stores data in the customer-selected hosting region; this VDPA limits storage to the United States or Canada. Baseline 6.2 permits access from outside the region, including Manila; this VDPA has no access term, so access from other locations is not addressed.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.summary: Vendor must maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed CIS Critical Security Controls Implementation Group 2.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 4.1 requires the measures described in Annex 2 and lets ExampleCo update them if security is not materially reduced; this VDPA sets a CIS Controls benchmark and states no update right.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.summary: Vendor must encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.scope: Covers Retailer Data at rest and in transit.
commitments.deviation: Baseline Annex 2 specifies AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit; this VDPA requires only industry-standard encryption without naming algorithms or versions.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services each year and provide it to Retailer within fifteen (15) days after Retailer's request.
commitments.summary: Vendor must obtain a SOC 2 Type II report each year and provide it to Retailer within 15 days after Retailer requests it.

deadline.anchor: Retailer's request

commitments.scope: Covers the Services.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 4.2 requires maintaining SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 certification; this VDPA requires a yearly SOC 2 Type II report, provided within 15 days of request, and does not mention ISO 27001.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not allow any Subprocessor not listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.scope: Covers any Subprocessor, including Vendor Affiliates, processing Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 5.1 grants general authorization to engage Subprocessors listed on the Trust Center; this VDPA requires Retailer's prior written consent for any Subprocessor not listed in Appendix B.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data.
commitments.summary: Vendor must request Retailer's written consent for a new Subprocessor at least 30 days before that Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data.

deadline.anchor: the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data

commitments.deviation: Baseline 5.2 requires notice of a new Subprocessor 30 days ahead by updating the Trust Center and emailing subscribers; this VDPA requires a written consent request 30 days ahead and no Trust Center posting.

commitments.quote: Retailer's silence is not consent.
commitments.summary: Retailer's silence does not count as consent to a new Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 5.3 gives Customer a 15-day objection right with termination as the sole remedy; this VDPA has no objection period and requires affirmative consent for a new Subprocessor.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA
commitments.summary: Vendor must bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as the VDPA.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: and remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.summary: Vendor remains liable for the acts and omissions of each Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 5.5 makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations; this VDPA makes Vendor liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions, which is broader.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Vendor must notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Vendor becomes aware of the Data Incident (the contract does not define awareness)

commitments.recipient: Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182, per Section 6.2
commitments.scope: Data Incidents as defined in Section 2.3, including incidents at a Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 7.1 allows 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a breach; this VDPA requires notice within 24 hours after Vendor becomes aware of any actual or reasonably suspected Data Incident.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182.
commitments.summary: Vendor must send Data Incident notice by email to Retailer Security Operations and by telephone to the listed number.
commitments.recipient: Retailer Security Operations, email secops@arg.example, telephone +1 (614) 555-0182
commitments.deviation: Baseline 7.2 sends notice to the security contact designated in the admin console, or to the account owner if none; this VDPA fixes email and telephone to Retailer Security Operations.

commitments.quote: Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Notice sent only to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy the 24-hour notice duty.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 7.2 falls back to the account owner when no security contact is designated; this VDPA says notice to account or procurement contacts does not satisfy the notice duty.

commitments.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
commitments.summary: Vendor's incident notice must describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps taken.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 7.3 describes only what is known, including data categories and measures taken or proposed; this VDPA requires identifying the Retailer Data and any Subprocessor involved and the steps taken, with no known-facts qualifier.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.summary: Vendor must supplement the incident notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 7.3 says ExampleCo will provide further information as it becomes available; this VDPA frames it as supplementing the notice.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, unless required by law.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents involving Retailer Data; exception for disclosures required by law.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation
commitments.summary: Vendor must cooperate with Retailer's investigation of a Data Incident.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents as defined in Section 2.3.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 7.3 only provides further information as it becomes available; this VDPA also requires cooperation with Retailer's investigation.

commitments.quote: shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.summary: Vendor must bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent Vendor or its Subprocessors caused it.
commitments.scope: Costs to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after the Subscription Agreement ends, Vendor shall delete all Retailer Data
commitments.summary: Vendor must delete all Retailer Data within 30 days after the Subscription Agreement ends.

deadline.anchor: the Subscription Agreement ends

commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including derived data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 10.1 allows 90 days after termination or expiry and 35 further days for backup overwrites; this VDPA requires deletion within 30 days and does not mention backups.

commitments.quote: and confirm the deletion to Retailer in writing.
commitments.summary: Vendor must confirm the deletion of Retailer Data to Retailer in writing.

deadline.anchor: the Subscription Agreement ends

commitments.deviation: Baseline 10.2 provides deletion certification only on Customer's written request; this VDPA requires written confirmation of deletion without a request.

commitments.quote: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with this VDPA once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice
commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with the VDPA once per calendar year on 30 days' notice.

deadline.anchor: the audit

commitments.deviation: Baseline 9.3 gives one on-site audit per 12 months on 60 days' notice, only where a supervisory authority requires it, and treats the SOC 2 and penetration test reports as satisfying audit rights; this VDPA gives an annual audit on 30 days' notice with none of those limits.

commitments.quote: and within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident.
commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance within 10 days after notice following a Data Incident.

deadline.anchor: Retailer's notice following a Data Incident

commitments.scope: Data Incidents as defined in Section 2.3.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: This VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.summary: The VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: A change of control of Vendor, by merger, acquisition or otherwise, does not terminate or modify this VDPA.
commitments.summary: A change of control of Vendor does not terminate or modify the VDPA.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.summary: An acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.scope: Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Amazon Web Services, Inc. | Hosting | United States
commitments.summary: Amazon Web Services, Inc. is an approved Subprocessor for hosting, located in the United States.
commitments.scope: Hosting of Retailer Data in the United States.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 5.1 relies on a published Trust Center list; this VDPA fixes the approved Subprocessor in Appendix B with a United States location.

commitments.quote: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. | Support ticketing | United States
commitments.summary: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. is an approved Subprocessor for support ticketing, located in the United States.
commitments.scope: Support ticketing for Retailer Data in the United States.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 5.1 relies on a published Trust Center list; this VDPA fixes the approved Subprocessor in Appendix B with a United States location.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) | Platform hosting and AI features for the Services | United States
commitments.summary: Amendment No. 1 adds ExampleCo, Inc., a Vendor Affiliate, as an approved Subprocessor for platform hosting and AI features in the United States.
commitments.scope: Platform hosting and AI features for the Services, located in the United States.
commitments.deviation: Baseline 8.3 lists AI model providers as Subprocessors on the Trust Center; this amendment adds the Vendor Affiliate ExampleCo by written amendment dated September 8, 2025, with a United States location. Baseline 6.2 allows access from Manila; the amendment states only a United States location.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
commitments.summary: This Addendum overrides conflicting terms in the Agreement, order forms, and any Supplier data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document.
commitments.deviation: Baseline DPA 11.1 makes the DPA control over the Agreement; this Addendum controls over the Agreement, order forms, and any DPA, privacy policy, or other Supplier document.

commitments.quote: Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Terms incorporated by reference from a Supplier website, including a trust or security site, bind neither Bank nor this Addendum.
commitments.deviation: Baseline DPA routes the SOC 2 report and pen test summary through the Trust Center; this Addendum states that Trust Center terms do not bind Bank.

commitments.quote: "Bank Data" means all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement, including (a) data provided by or on behalf of Bank or its customers; (b) metadata, logs and configuration data relating to Bank's use of the Services; and (c) any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized.
commitments.summary: Bank Data covers all data in any form handled by Supplier or a Subcontractor, including metadata, logs, and derived, aggregated or de-identified data.
commitments.scope: All data in any form that Supplier or a Subcontractor handles under the Agreement, including metadata, logs, model outputs and de-identified or aggregated derivatives.
commitments.deviation: Baseline covers only Personal Data contained in Customer Data; this Addendum covers all data in any form, including metadata, logs and derived data that is de-identified or aggregated.

commitments.quote: "Discovery" means the earliest time at which Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of a Security Incident.
commitments.summary: Discovery is the earliest time Supplier or a Subcontractor knew or should have known of a Security Incident, and it starts the notice clocks.
commitments.deviation: Baseline clock turns on ExampleCo's confirmation of a breach; this Addendum starts the clock at actual or constructive knowledge, which can be earlier.

commitments.quote: "Security Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected (a) unauthorized access to, or acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration or destruction of, Bank Data; or (b) unauthorized access to any system of Supplier or any Subcontractor that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data, whether or not unauthorized access to Bank Data has been confirmed.
commitments.summary: A Security Incident includes actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to or use of Bank Data and unauthorized access to systems holding Bank Data, whether or not confirmed.
commitments.scope: Actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to or use of Bank Data, and unauthorized access to any Supplier or Subcontractor system that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline Personal Data Breach requires ExampleCo confirmation and excludes unsuccessful attempts; this Addendum covers reasonably suspected incidents, needs no confirmation, and does not exclude unsuccessful attempts.
